data.description:
## Summary

The `rebar` **MCP server**'s `review_plan` tool cannot run the LLM passes because the
server process's Python environment is missing the AWS Bedrock provider package. The
review falls back to the deterministic floor and returns an unsigned `INDETERMINATE`
verdict, so **no plan-review attestation is minted** and the claim gate cannot be
satisfied through the MCP surface — even though the repo's own `.venv` has the provider
installed and the local CLI can run the review.

## Environment

- Host: macOS, repo checkout `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar`.
- MCP server: the configured `rebar` MCP server (tool `rebar-review_plan`).
- Configured model/runner: `runner: pydantic_ai`, `model: bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. From an MCP client, call `review_plan` on any reviewable ticket (observed on story
   `6f74-2795-5ad4-4a56` / `unemployed-saddened-peccary`).
2. Observe the returned verdict JSON.

## Actual behaviour

`review_plan` returns:

```
"verdict": "INDETERMINATE",
"coverage": { "llm_ran": false, "llm_unavailable": true,
  "llm_error": "a bedrock model/provider is configured but the optional bedrock provider
   package is not installed: pip install 'pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]'" },
"signature": { "signed": false, "reason": "INDETERMINATE" }
```

The deterministic floor (P1–P11) runs and passes; only the LLM layer is unavailable. No
signed PASS attestation is produced.

## Expected behaviour

The MCP server's `review_plan` runs the four-pass LLM review and (on a non-blocking PASS)
signs a plan-review attestation, matching the behaviour other sessions get and the local
repo-venv CLI (`.venv/bin/rebar review-plan`), whose interpreter has `pydantic_ai` with
Bedrock support available (verified: `importlib.util.find_spec('pydantic_ai.models.bedrock')`
is truthy; `pydantic_ai 1.107.2`).

## Root-cause hypothesis

The MCP server is launched from a Python environment (a global/stale install, not the repo
`.venv`) that lacks the `[agents]` Bedrock extra, i.e. `pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]` is not
installed for the server's interpreter. This is the exact failure mode
`docs/local-dev-env.md` warns about: running a build that predates / omits the optional
extras degrades `review-plan` / `verify-completion`. The MCP server must be started from a
build with the `[agents]` extra (e.g. the repo `.venv` provisioned via `make install`, which
runs `uv sync --locked --extra dev`).

## Impact

Plan-review (a certified claim gate op) cannot be completed through the MCP surface on this
box, so the documented "route tracker ops through the MCP server" path yields no attestation;
work must fall back to the local repo-venv CLI to review and sign.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The MCP server's launch environment has the Bedrock provider available: running
  `python -c "import importlib.util as u; assert u.find_spec('pydantic_ai.models.bedrock')"`
  against the server's interpreter exits 0 (checked on the box that hosts the MCP server).
- [ ] `review_plan` via the MCP server on a reviewable ticket returns a verdict with
  `coverage.llm_ran = true` (no `llm_unavailable`) and, on a non-blocking PASS, a signed
  attestation (`signature.signed = true`) — checked by re-running the tool and inspecting the
  returned JSON.
- [ ] The fix/runbook records how the MCP server's interpreter is pinned to a build carrying
  the `[agents]` extra (e.g. launched from the repo `.venv` per `docs/local-dev-env.md`), so
  the regression cannot silently recur.

## Notes

- Not a plan defect and not a code defect in `src/rebar` — an MCP-server **deployment/env**
  provisioning gap. The deterministic floor and the local CLI review path both work.
- Evidence captured from a live `review_plan` call on 2026-08-27.
data.title: rebar MCP server: review_plan returns INDETERMINATE (llm_unavailable) — bedrock provider package missing in server env
